question: Has anyone from the vendor given inconsistent answers about the product?

resolution.read_instruction: Extract every factual claim OrbitFlow staff make about the product: plans/tiers and what each includes, features, connectors/integrations, security/compliance, pricing, roadmap, and data handling, including hedges, corrections, and retractions. Note the speaker's role and the exact wording of each claim so claims can later be compared across calls for contradictions.
assumptions: The question concerns all sales calls in the catalogue, so no call type or company filter is applied.
'Inconsistent answers' is interpreted as contradictory or changed factual claims about the product, which requires comparing statements across calls.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: Growth starts at eighteen hundred a month, that's up to thirty users, annual agreement. Enterprise is custom — that's where the governance and security capabilities sit, plus higher usage.
findings.context: Growth plan starts at $1,800 a month for up to thirty users on an annual agreement; Enterprise is custom and is where governance and security capabilities sit, plus higher usage. — Pricing and tier contents stated by the AE when asked for rough cost; later the AE says no exact number until user model is known.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: I don't want to give you a number before I know your user model, because that's exactly where proposals become misleading.
findings.context: AE says she will not give a number until the user model is known, calling any number otherwise misleading. — Hedge on pricing, contrasting with the earlier Growth price figure.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: Builders and full workspace users are the licensed users. Approval-only or notification-only can be structured differently depending on the package. I'm deliberately not giving you an exact number today
findings.context: Builders and full workspace users are the licensed users; approval-only or notification-only users can be structured differently depending on the package. No exact number given. — Per-seat licensing hedge; customer asked for explicit approver seat treatment.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Enterprise customers can disable AI features outright. We log the model configuration used for a run. And we don't use customer workflow content to train a shared OrbitFlow model.
findings.context: AI features can be disabled outright on Enterprise; admins can restrict allowed models; OrbitFlow does not use customer workflow content to train a shared model. — Data handling and AI claims; customer asked for this in writing.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Baseline is SOC 2 Type II. SAML SSO and SCIM on Enterprise. Encryption in transit and at rest. Audit logs cover administrative and workflow events.
findings.context: Baseline security: SOC 2 Type II; SAML SSO and SCIM on Enterprise; encryption in transit and at rest; audit logs for admin and workflow events; EU residency available on Enterprise. — Security and compliance claims; tiering of SSO/SCIM and residency to Enterprise.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Run events and metrics through APIs and webhooks, and audit export on Enterprise.
findings.context: Audit export is on Enterprise; run events and metrics are available through APIs and webhooks. — Monitoring integration claim; tier-gated audit export.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: On Enterprise you can package reusable JavaScript steps if you need to. There's a generic REST action and webhooks. We don't claim every workflow is no-code.
findings.context: Enterprise tier allows packaging reusable JavaScript steps; generic REST action and webhooks exist; AI steps are optional explicit steps; no claim that every workflow is no-code. — Feature/technical capability claims with tier gating.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: We cache metadata but refresh it, and mapping errors surface on the run.
findings.context: Mapping errors surface on the run and users can alert when error rates cross a threshold; metadata is cached and refreshed. Vendor hedges that schema change handling is not guaranteed and recommends explicit validation. — Schema change handling claim, hedged.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: For your stack it's a mix of native connectors and API-based options. What I'd want to do in a pilot is validate each required operation rather than just point at a logo on our integrations page.
findings.context: Integrations: native connectors and API-based options; a pilot will validate each required operation rather than rely on the integrations page logo list. Private-network calls depend on environment and may need an agent or gateway; not assumed. — Connector claims, explicitly hedged.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: We do support role-based access, workspace separation, and secrets aren't displayed in run logs.
findings.context: Secrets are not displayed in run logs; role-based access and workspace separation are supported; field-level masking should be part of security design rather than promised now. — Access control claim with explicit hedge on field-level masking.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: SOC 2 Type II is the baseline. SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, both on Enterprise. Encryption in transit and at rest. Audit logs covering administrative and workflow events. Retention configurable within supported ranges. EU data residency available on Enterprise.
findings.context: OrbitFlow staff (Jon Bell) states baseline certifications and features: SOC 2 Type II baseline, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning on Enterprise, encryption in transit and at rest, audit logs, retention configurable within supported ranges, EU data residency available on Enterprise. — Vendor product/security claim during security section; Enterprise-tier gating stated.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Default depends on where the workspace is provisioned. I'd rather confirm the specifics in writing than guess at your architecture on a call.
findings.context: Vendor declined to confirm default data region, deferring to written answer. — Hedge on data residency; contrasts with the Enterprise EU residency claim in T014.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: I'm not going to give you a yes on this call. What I will do is get you a written answer from our legal and compliance side within
findings.context: Vendor would not confirm a BAA on the call; will provide written position from legal/compliance within about a week. — BAA is the gating item for the prospect; vendor explicitly refused a verbal yes.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: We publish the list and there's a notification mechanism for changes. The exact notice period is contractual
findings.context: Vendor says subprocessors are published with a change notification mechanism; exact notice period is contractual. — Subprocessor disclosure claim, deferred to documents.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Per-workspace granularity I'd want to check against your specific requirement, because there are limits.
findings.context: Retention is configurable within supported ranges but per-workspace granularity and floor are unconfirmed; vendor declined to quote a number. — Hedge on retention limits; later to be put in pack.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: We also don't use customer workflow content to train a shared OrbitFlow model.
findings.context: Vendor describes AI steps as explicit workflow steps, admins can restrict models, Enterprise can disable AI features, model config is logged per run, and customer workflow content is not used to train a shared model. — LLM data handling claim; prospect asked whether it is in the contract.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: It needs to be in the contract for you to rely on it
findings.context: Vendor says the no-training commitment must be in the contract to rely on it. — Maya acknowledges the claim needs contractual backing; no contract language confirmed.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: If you need field-level masking for specific payloads, that's a design conversation rather than a checkbox.
findings.context: Vendor says field-level masking is a design conversation, not a checkbox; run logs never display secrets; support access is controlled and logged. — Data-access security claim; vendor hedged against overclaiming masking.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Run events and metrics via APIs and webhooks, and audit export on Enterprise.
findings.context: Vendor says run events and metrics are available via APIs and webhooks, and audit export is on Enterprise. — Audit log export to SIEM; Enterprise gating.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Workspace separation is supported, and Enterprise has stronger governance around who can publish where.
findings.context: Vendor says workspace separation is supported and Enterprise has stronger governance; logical separation described as supportable. — Environment separation claim.

findings.quote: Growth starts at eighteen hundred a month for up to thirty users on an annual agreement. Enterprise is custom-priced
findings.context: Vendor pricing: Growth starts at 1800 a month for up to thirty users on annual agreement; Enterprise is custom-priced and includes advanced governance, security capabilities, and higher usage. Prospect deemed an Enterprise fit. — Commercial claim; Enterprise tier scope stated.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: Builders and full workspace users are the licensed ones. Approval-only or notification-only can be structured differently depending on package.
findings.context: Vendor declined to give a seat/license figure; licensing depends on builders vs full users, and approval-only or notification-only users can be structured differently depending on package. — Licensing/per-seat model; vendor deliberately withheld a figure.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: On Enterprise you can package reusable JavaScript steps. There's a generic REST action and webhooks. We don't claim every workflow is no-code.
findings.context: Vendor says Enterprise can package reusable JavaScript steps; there is a generic REST action and webhooks; not every workflow is no-code. — Feature and technical-depth claim, with explicit hedge.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: We cache metadata but refresh it, and mapping errors surface on the run.
findings.context: Vendor says mapping errors surface on the run and cached metadata is refreshed; error-rate alerting is available. — Schema change handling claim.

findings.quote: It's not impossible. It's API work.
findings.context: Vendor said integrations are validated per required operation in a pilot and not via a logo page; Databricks described as API work rather than native. — Connector claim, hedged; Databricks not phase one.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Version history and change metadata, yes. Rollback and promotion patterns vary by workflow and package.
findings.context: Vendor said version history and change metadata exist; rollback and promotion patterns vary by workflow and package. — Version control claim with hedge.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: a valid outcome is "don't buy OrbitFlow" if the existing approach meets the criteria more cheaply.
findings.context: Vendor stated Jon's summary that the blocker is regulatory; in the earlier turn Maya had said the BAA would be answered within a week and that a valid outcome is not buying. — Maya's framing of pricing and outcome; no contradiction found in this call's vendor statements beyond the hedged answers.

findings.quote: I believe the Shopify integration is native and event-driven, but I'm not going to swear to the exact trigger coverage without checking.
findings.context: OrbitFlow's Shopify integration is native and event-driven, though the vendor will not confirm exact trigger coverage without checking. — Vendor hedge on a connector claim; later promised a written answer from Nina (solutions engineer). Hedged, not a firm product claim.

findings.context: EU data residency is available on the Enterprise plan; the default processing region on Growth is unconfirmed and will be confirmed in writing. — Security/data handling claim with a hedge on the Growth tier. Customer then confirmed they would consider the expensive Enterprise tier.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Growth starts at eighteen hundred a month, up to thirty users, on an annual agreement.
findings.context: Growth plan starts at £1,800 a month (quoted as eighteen hundred), up to thirty users, on an annual agreement. — Pricing and plan limits stated by vendor; customer later confirmed the figure as twenty-one-six, implying a currency/VAT conversion, which the vendor did not address.

findings.context: An annual prepay gives a meaningful discount on the Growth price, but not a halving of cost. — Pricing hedge on discount size; vendor explicitly rules out a large reduction.

findings.quote: Usage is scoped on workflow runs and premium connectors. I'd want to model that for your volumes rather than say "no" and surprise you later.
findings.context: Usage is scoped on workflow runs and premium connectors, and pricing for the customer's volumes will be modelled rather than stated as 'no' cost. — Vendor hedge on additional usage costs; said assumptions would be put in writing.

findings.quote: It's not that we do things Zapier can't. It's that sixty independent Zaps is sixty things to maintain and this is more like eight.
findings.context: Reusable subflows reduce sixty independent automations to roughly eight maintained pieces; the vendor says it does not do things Zapier cannot. — Feature/roadmap-style product claim about templates and reusable components; the 'eight' is a vendor estimate.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: It's optional steps inside a workflow — classification, summarisation, extracting fields out of text, drafting something a human then approves. It's not an autonomous agent thing.
findings.context: OrbitFlow offers an AI option of optional workflow steps (classification, summarisation, field extraction, drafting for human approval), not an autonomous agent; source references can be stored alongside generated output. — Feature claim on AI capabilities; vendor said they would underplay it.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: You'd get one. That's not extra cost, it's just how it's structured.
findings.context: Version history and change metadata are available on every workflow, and publish-to-production versus dev-workspace permissions can be defined; a dev workspace is included at no extra cost. — Feature claim on governance; the no-extra-cost statement on the dev workspace is a pricing claim.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Yes — you can alert when error rates cross a threshold.
findings.context: Alerts can be configured on error rates crossing a threshold rather than per individual failure. — Monitoring feature confirmed in response to customer question.

findings.context: SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported, both on the Enterprise tier. — Vendor's direct answer to the customer's governance list (SAML, SCIM).

findings.quote: EU data residency is available on Enterprise.
findings.context: EU data residency is available on Enterprise. — Vendor answer to the customer's request for German or EU data residency.

findings.quote: EU. I am not going to tell you we have a German region because we don't.
findings.context: OrbitFlow has EU data residency but no German region. — Clarification after the customer asked 'German or EU. Which is it?'; vendor narrowed the claim.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: SOC 2 Type II is our baseline.
findings.context: SOC 2 Type II is the baseline, and pen test and DR documentation are available under the normal security process. — Security/compliance claims; the pen test and DR documentation were offered as available, not yet shared.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Run events and metrics through APIs and webhooks, and audit export on Enterprise.
findings.context: Audit export is available on Enterprise, and run events and metrics can be sent through APIs and webhooks. — Answer to the customer's question on exporting audit data to their own systems.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: And we don't use customer workflow content to train a shared OrbitFlow model.
findings.context: Enterprise customers can disable AI features and restrict allowed models; the platform does not use customer workflow content to train a shared model. — AI and data-handling claims; the customer said the no-training point needs to be contractual.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Secret values are not displayed in run logs, no.
findings.context: Secret values are not displayed in run logs. — Credential handling claim, in answer to the customer's question about secrets in logs.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: Growth is eighteen hundred a month up to thirty users on an annual agreement, but that's not your shape.
findings.context: Growth plan is priced at 1,800 a month for up to thirty users on an annual agreement; the vendor said this is not the customer's tier, which is Enterprise. — Pricing claim; the vendor stated the Growth price and placed the customer on Enterprise, custom priced.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: Builders and full workspace users are the licensed users.
findings.context: Builders and full workspace users are the licensed users; approval-only or notification-only users can be structured differently depending on package. — Licensing model; the vendor declined to give a number until the user model is defined.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: What I will not do is tell you there's a one-click SAP connector that solves your estate, because your estate is not one thing.
findings.context: There is no one-click SAP connector; SAP connectivity uses API-based options, the generic REST action, or an agent/gateway pattern. — Connector claim that explicitly disclaims a turnkey SAP connector.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Field-level masking for specific payloads is a design conversation rather than a checkbox
findings.context: Field-level masking for specific payloads is a design conversation, not a standard feature. — Hedge on a security capability; vendor declined to say 'yes, masking'.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: Administrators can restrict which models are allowed. Enterprise customers can disable AI features entirely.
findings.context: Enterprise customers can disable AI features entirely; administrators can restrict which models are allowed. — OrbitFlow's AI governance answer to Hannah's model-risk gate. Nina says she will confirm per-workspace granularity in writing (T028), which was not confirmed on the call.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: and you have full control over whether you use it at all. AI steps are explicit, inspectable steps inside a workflow. They're not ambient and they're not in the execution path unless you put them there.
findings.context: The customer has full control over whether AI is used at all, and AI steps are not in the execution path unless the customer puts them there. — Opening AI-governance claim. Later (T038) Nina says AI-output containment is only a design convention, not a platform constraint.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: Today it's a design convention plus review, not a hard platform constraint. I'm not going to tell you there's a switch labelled "AI outputs cannot feed decisions", because there isn't.
findings.context: AI outputs cannot be enforced as leaf nodes that never feed decisions; this is a design convention plus review, not a hard platform constraint. — Contrasts with the earlier 'full control' framing (T026). Hannah asks for it to be recorded as a known limitation (T201).

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: SAML SSO and SCIM on Enterprise. ... EU data residency available on Enterprise.
findings.context: SAML SSO and SCIM, and EU data residency, are available on the Enterprise tier. — Security and compliance claims tied to the Enterprise plan. Leo says the Enterprise tier includes security capabilities (T145).

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: And we don't use customer workflow content to train a shared OrbitFlow model.
findings.context: OrbitFlow does not use customer workflow content to train a shared OrbitFlow model. — Data-handling claim. Hannah asks whether it is contractual or marketing; Leo says it must be contractual (T045).

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: I'll open a run — and you get every step, its inputs, its outputs, timing, retries, and any human approval with who approved and when.
findings.context: Run history records every step with its inputs, outputs, timing, retries, and any human approval with who approved and when; a timed-out, retried, remediated run appears as one record. — Demo of run history. The claim that the original value is retained is qualified in T083.

findings.quote: So yes, but I want to be precise: that's because this approval was configured to collect a structured input. If someone had just clicked approve, there'd be nothing to compare.
findings.context: The original value is only visible for comparison if the approval was configured to collect a structured input; a plain approve click leaves nothing to compare. — Self-qualification of the earlier demo claim that 'all of that is one record' (T079). Nina says 'I want to be precise'. Hannah concludes it depends on workflow design (T084).

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: So when something fails, you're debugging a twelve-step subflow, not step forty of sixty.
findings.context: Subflows allow debugging a twelve-step subflow rather than step forty of sixty; subflows can be run in isolation with a given input, but this is not a full unit test. — Composition claim that answers the debugging concern raised at the start. Nina does not claim it meets Hannah's unit-test definition (T097).

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: The others are a mix of native connectors and API options, and I'd validate each required operation in a pilot rather than pointing at logos.
findings.context: Connector coverage is mixed (native connectors and API options) and must be validated per required operation in a pilot rather than assumed from logos. — Hedge on the integration list. findings.context: Workspace separation is supported; the exact granularity of per-workspace AI disablement is unconfirmed and will be answered in writing. — Hedged answer. Nina says 'I believe yes' and declines to guess.

findings.context: Growth plan is eighteen hundred a month up to thirty users on an annual agreement; Enterprise is custom priced and adds advanced governance, security capabilities, and higher usage. — Pricing and tier claims. Leo says the customer is not a Growth shape.

findings.context: OrbitFlow staff said the Growth package is eighteen hundred a month, up to thirty users, on an annual agreement. — Vendor pricing and tier contents for the Growth package.

findings.quote: The thirty is the package, so the price is the price.

findings.quote: All of those are native connectors, no problem at all.
findings.context: OrbitFlow staff said all listed connectors (HubSpot, Slack, Google, Asana, Sheets) are native, and that the product is completely no-code. — Connector and no-code claims; later the staff said the date-slip alert might need two workflows and an SE check, and that the pod customisation is just configuration.

findings.quote: Possibly. I'd want to check with an SE, honestly. But it's definitely doable.

findings.context: OrbitFlow staff said the first use case could be set up in a couple of weeks and that a September launch is no problem. — Implementation timeline claim, made for the customer's September process launch.

findings.context: OrbitFlow's Dynamics 365 and Teams integration routes are API-based, plus a generic REST action and webhooks; Jon says they do not have the deepest first-class Dynamics connector on the market. — Vendor admits Dynamics gap; central to evaluation.
